# naming.variable.dictionary-missing-receiver-and-array-default-phases

Kind: `native-observation`

## Problem statement

An absent array root and a missing element of an existing array have different read-callback ordering. Array defaults and a write trace that unsets the element further separate the stored value from the result of append, dictionary append or increment; a generic read-modify-write model can silently use the wrong receiver or return a retired value.

## Question

What final result, callback order and array/default state do the exact 18 original scripts report for missing receivers, C9 array defaults and write-trace destruction?

## Conclusion

The retained existing-array cases report read then write and use the callback-created dictionary; absent-root cases report write only. The C9 default controls retain the independent default and produce the stated appended/incremented values. C9 write-trace destruction completes normally with an empty returned value and no element. These are measured script results, not physical receiver/cache or arbitrary normal-write proofs.

## Scope

Exact 18 ASCII scripts/results retained as hexadecimal controls.tsv rows: two each C8.5.19/C8.6.18 and seven each C9.0.4/C9.1.0. Original manifest identifies versions but no executable/build hashes or original presenter. C8.4, Jim and BIG-IP were not queried in this capture; their absence is not an unsupported result.
